issues.legal_issue: A prompt first report with explained omissions and differences does not, by itself, discredit eyewitness testimony.
material_facts: An eyewitness reported the incident promptly and stated that two identified assailants arrived with several people whose names were unknown to him.
At trial, the eyewitness gave a fuller account of the assailants and their weapons; a supplementary statement adding details was recorded at the police station soon after the first report.

The tractor driver remained at the driver’s seat and was not known to the eyewitness, and the court found that the first report’s description of the group could account for the apparent difference in numbers.
Two other sons of the deceased remained some distance from the shooting and did not attempt to intervene.
issues.conclusion: The differences between the first report and the trial testimony did not discredit the eyewitness account; the court accepted the explanation for the omissions and found the witnesses’ presence at the incident credible.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the first report and testimony in light of the circumstances, including the report’s promptness, the eyewitness’s lack of familiarity with some persons, and the explained distance of witnesses from the shooting. It relied on no cited statutory provision or earlier case for this assessment.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.prompt_first_report: An eyewitness gave a report of the incident promptly after it occurred.
predicates.unfamiliarity_explains_omissions: The eyewitness was unfamiliar with some people involved, providing an explanation for omissions or incomplete descriptions in the first report.
predicates.circumstances_explain_witnesses_not_inte: The circumstances, including the witnesses’ distance from the violence, explain why they did not intervene.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction is appealed, a prompt first report and circumstances explaining its omissions or the witnesses’ conduct mean the eyewitness testimony is not discredited.

issues.legal_issue: Corroborated eyewitness accounts and reliable forensic linkage can sustain convictions despite challenges to identification, participation, or the handling of physical evidence.
material_facts: Two eyewitnesses testified to the shooting, and the court found their accounts mutually corroborative and not undermined in cross-examination.
The eyewitness evidence was corroborated by fired cartridge cases recovered from the scene and by firearms later recovered from the accused and the tractor driver.
The cartridge cases and firearms reached the forensic laboratory sealed, and testing linked cartridge cases to the recovered firearms.
The court rejected the claim that the cartridge cases had been tampered with or planted, noting that they reached the laboratory before the firearms were recovered.
The court found the evidence against the appellants sufficient even without relying on the tractor driver’s evidence.
issues.conclusion: The evidence was sufficient to uphold the appellants’ convictions, and the appeals against conviction were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered the eyewitness evidence together with the forensic evidence linking recovered cartridge cases to recovered firearms, and found the recovery and handling evidence reliable. It stated that the evidence apart from the tractor driver’s testimony was sufficient. No earlier case was relied on, and no specific evidentiary provision was cited; the convictions had been entered under Sections 302 read with 149 and 148 of the Indian Penal Code.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.corroborated_eyewitness_accounts: More than one eyewitness gave accounts that corroborated each other and were not materially discredited.
predicates.reliable_forensic_linkage: Physical evidence was reliably handled and forensic testing linked evidence from the scene to firearms recovered from persons implicated in the offence.

issues.definition: In an appeal from conviction, corroborated eyewitness accounts and reliable forensic linkage mean the conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence is not reduced where no mitigating circumstances are established in the record.
material_facts: The appellants challenged the death sentences and asked that they be reduced to imprisonment for life.
The court found no force in that request and observed that any mitigating circumstances not placed on the record could be brought to the appropriate government.
issues.conclusion: The court did not reduce the death sentences; it stated that any mitigating circumstances absent from the record should be brought to the appropriate government.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to reduce the sentences in the absence of mitigating circumstances shown in the record and identified the appropriate government as the avenue for presenting unrecorded mitigating circumstances. It relied on no cited statutory provision or earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_challenging_death_sentence: The proceeding challenges a death sentence imposed for a criminal offence.
predicates.no_mitigating_circumstances_in_record: The record does not establish mitigating circumstances supporting a reduction of the sentence.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a death sentence and the record establishes no mitigating circumstances, the sentence is not reduced.

issues.legal_issue: A review petition seeking reconsideration of a summary refusal of special leave has no occasion to succeed when the related appeals are dismissed and no basis for review is established.
material_facts: A petitioner sought review of an earlier summary dismissal of a petition for special leave.
The court dismissed the related appeals after finding no force in them and concluded that there was no occasion to review the earlier order.
issues.legal_principle: The court found no occasion to review its earlier summary order in light of its disposition of the related appeals. It relied on no cited statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.review_petition_against_summary_special_: The proceeding seeks review of a summary dismissal of a petition for special leave.
predicates.related_appeals_dismissed: The appeals arising from the same judgment are dismissed.
predicates.no_review_basis_found: The court finds no basis requiring review of the earlier order.

issues.definition: When a review petition challenges a summary special-leave dismissal, the related appeals are dismissed, and no review basis is found, the review petition is dismissed.
